## Relationships

- **Parent:** #5 (Phase-4 tile spill)
- **Blocked by:** #8 (WP1 spill/fetch/compose ABI)
- **Blocks:** none. Phase-4 `ready` in `dual-host-parity.json` waits on this plus #8.
- **Related:** #22 (use the stream handle when it exists; do not implement `stream.rs` here), #23 (host-neutral client path; this issue is spill engagement), #18 (will have landed before #8), #24, #10, #11
- **Non-goals:** tile store implementation (#8); `stream.rs` (#22); npm `@curatelabs/xyg` (#23)

Part of #5 (Phase 4: Tier-3 disk-resident 256² tile spill) — WP2. Blocked on WP1 ABI.

## Objective

Wire the Phase-4 tile-spill ABI into both hosts with identical behavior (parity is identity, not convention), keeping hosts thin: policy lives in Rust, hosts pass buffers and record decisions.

## Scope

**Python (`python/xy/`)**

- [ ] `_native.py`: bind the new entry points; `ABI_VERSION` bumped in lock-step with `src/lib.rs`.
- [ ] `config.py`: add `PYRAMID_RESIDENT_BYTES` (default per WP0) alongside the existing pyramid knobs (`PYRAMID_MIN_POINTS`, `PYRAMID_BASE_DIM`, `PYRAMID_NO_RESCAN_ROWS`, `PYRAMID_MAX_DIM`).
- [ ] `interaction._ensure_pyramid` / `_payload._density_trace_spec` / `density_view`: engage spill behind memmap / `n > PYRAMID_NO_RESCAN_ROWS` / explicit `pyramid_spill=True`; first paint and `density_view` prefer spilled tiles when the resident pyramid would exceed budget. This closes the current cliff where an adaptive `PYRAMID_MAX_DIM=16384` base (~1.33 GB counts + ~2.7 GB color) sits entirely in RAM.
- [ ] §28 recording: `binning: "pyramid-L<l>-tiles"` plus tiles hit / miss / resident bytes on every reply; `pyramid_report_bytes` covers tile-store residency so `Figure.pyramid_bytes` stays truthful.
- [ ] Weakref finalizer frees the tile store (and its disk artifacts per WP0 lifecycle) exactly as `pyramid_free` does today.

**Node (`packages/xy-node/`)**

- [ ] `src/native.js` + `src/pyramid.js`: mirror bindings, constants, `shouldUsePyramid`/`densityViewFromPyramid` spill engagement, and §28 recording.
- [ ] `figure.js` density emit prefers spilled tiles under the same conditions as Python.

**Parity**

- [ ] Python ↔ Node golden: identical spilled-figure inputs produce identical composed grids and identical recorded `binning`/residency stats.
- [ ] Update `spec/design/dual-host-parity.json` `lod_tiers` Phase-4 cell to `ready` only when both hosts land; matrix doc row updated.

## Acceptance

- `uv run pytest` additions cover engagement conditions, budget adherence, and recording (fixtures MB-scale; never 1B rows in CI).
- `packages/xy-node/test/pyramid.test.mjs` twin coverage.
- Existing Phase-3 tests unchanged and green — the in-RAM hot path must not regress.

body:
## Relationships

- **Parent:** #5 (Phase-4 tile spill)
- **Blocked by:** #18 (draft PR #19 paused; re-land inside `crates/xyg-engine`). WP0 (#7) is done.
- **Blocks:** #9 (WP2 hosts), #10 (optional WP3 tile-keyed client cache)
- **Related:** #22 (canonical f64 store — parallel after #18; prefer #22 first when both are free so fetch can read the stream handle, but do not wait on `stream.rs` to re-land this), #24, #19 (paused implementation), #23 (client packaging — not this)
- **Non-goals:** owning the canonical column store (#22); npm paint-client packaging (#23); crate split (#18)

Part of #5 (Phase 4: Tier-3 disk-resident 256² tile spill) — WP1. WP0 (#7) is done. **Blocked on #18** (draft PR #19 paused; re-land inside `crates/xyg-engine`). Not blocked on #22 (`stream.rs` is the canonical store; this issue is derived-cache spill).

## Objective

Implement the tile store in the Rust core: keyed 256² data-space tiles with disk spill/fetch, LRU residency under a byte budget, and compose-from-tiles. Rust owns residency end to end; hosts stay thin.

**This is a storage-layout change, not a wrapper.** The shipped `Pyramid` (`src/tiles.rs`) stores `levels: Vec<Vec<u32>>` — one contiguous grid per level — with optional `[u16; 4]` mean-color planes. Phase 4 re-plumbs that into `(level, tx, ty)`-keyed tiles that can spill and load independently while keeping the Phase-3 in-RAM path hot for traces that fit (roadmap non-goal: do not regress the resident fast path).

## Scope

- [ ] New `src/tile_store.rs` (or extension of `tiles.rs`): tile key `(level, tx, ty)`, on-disk layout per WP0 decision, LRU under `PYRAMID_RESIDENT_BYTES`, frame-pinning for the ≤ ceil(w/256+1)×ceil(h/256+1) tiles serving the current view.
- [ ] C ABI: `xy_pyramid_spill` / `xy_tile_fetch` / `xy_tiles_compose` (names per WP0). Bump `ABI_VERSION` (currently 57) in `src/lib.rs` **and** `python/xy/_native.py` together; mirror in `packages/xy-node/src/native.js`.
- [ ] Compose-from-tiles preserves Phase-3 semantics exactly: area-weighted downsample (#153 regression guard), source-cell-under-pixel upsample, `max_upsample` refusal, exact u64→u32 count reductions, alpha-weighted color means (≤ 0.5 lsb/level re-round stays the recorded bound).
- [ ] Zone-map-pruned tile index for unordered scatter (bucket at ingest) per WP0 design.
- [ ] Append: count-only dirty-tile rebuild across levels; colored tiles keep refuse-and-invalidate. Domain growth invalidates per WP0 spec.
- [ ] Residency stats surfaced through the ABI so hosts can record §28 `binning: "pyramid-L<l>-tiles"` + tiles hit / miss / resident bytes.

## Invariants (dossier — do not regress)

- §27: tiles are derived, rebuildable caches; canonical f64 (possibly memmap) stays the truth; every resident byte reported.
- §28: every residency/tier decision recorded, never silent.
- §32: replies stay screen-bounded regardless of dataset size; browser remains paint-only.
- §19: NaN never reaches any buffer handed to hosts; non-finite pairs ignored at bin time (parity with `bin_2d_counts`).
- Build-time transients stay within `kernels::MEAN_COLOR_ACCUM_BUDGET_BYTES` shedding behavior — spill must not reintroduce the 1B-colored-build OOM.

## Acceptance

- Rust unit tests: spill→fetch→compose golden equals the in-RAM compose for the same inputs; LRU keeps resident bytes ≤ budget under a synthetic access pattern; dirty-tile append equals full rebuild.
- `scripts/abi_smoke.py` extended for the new entry points (stdlib-only, no PyPI).
- Fixtures are MB-scale synthetic tile directories — CI never allocates 1B rows.

## Purpose

Stage 0 is the stop-the-line recovery gate for the XYG 0.6.0 release train. No M2 parity follow-on, feature milestone, packaging milestone, or release-candidate work may proceed while this tracker is open.

This tracker converts the current red `main` state into a bounded prerequisite rather than allowing graph, temporal, geospatial, out-of-core, packaging, or RC work to build on untrusted artifacts and evidence.

## Current evidence

- CI run 33681867226 fails the no-Rust wheel plus Linux x64, Linux arm64, and Windows x64 wheel verification after the Figure export hub split.
- CodSpeed run 33753290582 fails the factorization benchmark, the screen-bounded density first-payload contract, and the Node-authored Scene evidence path.
- PR #852 skipped wheel, sdist, no-Rust, benchmark, and cross-browser jobs; current branch protection requires only the central test, direct-browser/WASM foundation, and Python 3.11 floor checks.

## Children

- Restore release-blocking wheel and no-Rust artifact verification.
- Restore the screen-bounded density first-payload contract.
- Repair Node XYTA authored-Scene materialization and cross-host evidence.
- Repair CodSpeed benchmark harness drift and restore the complete benchmark run.
- Make release-surface CI required, non-skippable when relevant, and approval-governed.

The child issues are represented as native GitHub `blocked by` dependencies. This tracker closes only after all children close.

## Close when

- The latest commit on `main` has green CI, packaging, CodSpeed, and browser-evidence workflows.
- The complete required matrix succeeds three consecutive times on the same product state without a required job being silently skipped.
- Release-affecting changes cannot merge unless their artifact, host-parity, and evidence gates execute and pass.
- All child issues are closed with linked run and artifact evidence.

## Stop-the-line policy

While this tracker is open:

- Do not merge feature expansion for M4, M5, M6, M7, M8, or M9.
- M2 work is limited to this recovery gate and #855 host-parity completion.
- A broken `main` blocks feature merges until restored.
- Do not waive a failure by weakening an invariant or converting a required check to advisory without explicit human approval recorded on the owning issue.

## Milestone governance

Creating a milestone or moving an issue between milestones requires explicit human approval recorded in a GitHub issue or pull request. Agents and automation may propose an exact milestone change, but must not perform it before approval. Editing descriptions to record approved dependencies does not authorize moving issues.

## Related

- Host-parity completion: #855
- M2 landing: #852
- Failed CI: https://github.com/CurateLabs/xyg/actions/runs/33681867226
- Failed CodSpeed/evidence: https://github.com/CurateLabs/xyg/actions/runs/33753290582
- Release candidate: #108

body:
## Relationships

- **Parent:** #5 (Phase-4 tile spill)
- **Blocked by:** #8 Rust tile ABI and #9 host engagement (completed); consumes their `(level, tx, ty)` reply contract
- **Blocks:** none
- **Related:** #23 (uses the host-neutral client; does not own `@curatelabs/xyg` packaging), #9, #11, #24
- **Non-goals:** browser-owned residency; npm packaging; `stream.rs`

Part of #5 (Phase 4: Tier-3 disk-resident 256² tile spill) — WP3, required for Phase-4 exit. Also closes Phase-3 item 8 (`spec/design/lod-architecture.md`).

## Objective

Replace the window-keyed `densityCache` in `js/src/45_lod.ts` with a tile-keyed cache consuming `(level, tx, ty)`, so pan reuses textures instead of re-shipping whole windows. Today the kernel composes the whole window every time and the client caches by density window — "pan = tile reuse" is design, not behavior; this makes it behavior.

## Scope

- [ ] Tile-keyed texture cache keyed by `(level, tx, ty)`; same eviction budget and crossfade mechanics as the existing window cache (`_densitySwitchPrev` crossfades unchanged).
- [ ] Client reads the served level from the payload (it currently ignores it) and keys crossfades on level transitions.
- [ ] Pan ships only newly exposed edge tiles; zoom crossfades adjacent-level tile sets.
- [ ] Stays within the browser-client contract: WebGL2 paint/pick/gestures only — no layout/LOD/encode reimplementation, no `koffi`/`node:fs` imports; draws §29 buffers from any host.
- [ ] `node js/build.mjs` typecheck + bundle regeneration; bundles stay a generated, git-ignored artifact (§33).

## Non-goals

- Browser-side tile residency policy (Rust owns it; the client holds at most screen-bounded textures regardless — §32).
- Changing the R8-log / RGBA8 texture upload formats.

## Acceptance

- `scripts/render_smoke_nonumpy.py` / browser smoke extended: pan across a tiled density trace re-uses cached tiles (observable via recorded fetch counts) and produces pixel-identical frames vs the uncached path.
- No wire-format change beyond carrying tile keys + level (raw f32/typed buffers only — no JSON numbers, §29).

## Verification

Follow #108's shared lean CI policy: bounded correctness and affected integration checks in the existing Release surfaces aggregate; hosted performance/100M+ runs scheduled/manual, full platform evidence at release. Reuse hash-linked evidence; no duplicate gate or repeated-green-run requirement.

body:
## Tracker Purpose

Restore a trustworthy green main after regressions on commit `b7acef538d0cdfacb447654030ee513e7bf3569d` and stop release closure from advancing while hard correctness, artifact, compatibility, or evidence failures remain unresolved.

This is a regression gate for the v0.6.0 release train. It does not reopen the historical Stage 0 recovery record in #862 or create a new milestone.

## Current Regressions

- [ ] #1004 — native chrome slot styling is silently discarded.
- [ ] #1005 — packaged WASM assets are missing before CI/Bazel/benchmark consumers.
- [ ] #1006 — Matplotlib 3.11 reference compatibility has 13 failures.
- [ ] #1007 — typed-series fragmentation and browser-painter capacity rejection disagree with policy.
- [ ] #1008 — the required aggregate can pass despite applicable hard failures.

## Objective

Close every current-head regression with failing-before/passing-after automated coverage, restore green required workflows, and make the release gate detect recurrence without adding redundant CI ceremony.

## Close Criteria

- Every child is closed with linked implementation, test, specification, and run evidence.
- Current main has green CI, Bazel, browser evidence, and CodSpeed correctness execution; expensive timing comparisons may remain scheduled/advisory under #108 policy.
- `Release surfaces` fails when any applicable hard job fails or is silently skipped.
- Clean-checkout artifact consumers produce or verify every required generated asset.
- The release DAG and milestone descriptions identify this tracker as a blocking prerequisite.
- No acceptance criterion is waived by weakening a product invariant or merely changing an oracle.

## BDD Completion Scenarios

### Scenario: Current main is trustworthy
Given the exact accepted product commit
When required correctness, artifact, compatibility, browser, and benchmark-contract checks run
Then every applicable hard check passes
And the aggregate reports success only after those dependencies succeed.

### Scenario: A regression is caught before release
Given a deliberate recurrence of any child failure
When its smallest automated regression test and release gate run
Then the focused test fails
And the release tracker remains blocked.

## Testing

Each child owns focused unit/integration/browser coverage. This tracker owns the cross-workflow read-back: current-head runs, required aggregate propagation, clean-checkout proof, and native GitHub dependency audit.

## Documentation

Update affected `spec/` contracts and #108 evidence links. Preserve the lean CI policy.

## Non-Goals

- Creating a milestone.
- Requiring three identical green runs.
- Running the full platform/release matrix on every PR.
- Implementing unrelated feature milestones.

## Related Issues

- Historical recovery: #862
- Release tracker: #108
- Candidate conformance: #54
